messages.subject_clean: cforest and ctree
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to predict a dichotomous variable based on 24 input
variables of various types (continuous as well as discrete variable)
from a total of 3,623 observations.  I hope to identify variables of
importance, and then build a predictive model using ctree for
deployment, and to score on a new data set.

I am interested in finding what the variables of importance (varimp)
are.  The variable of importance is the conditional importance or
permutation importance, per defined by Strobl. et al.

I ran a conditional forest in Rattle (2.5.41) overnight and got
nowhere.  It appears it is extremely computationally intensive and
requires more than 4 GB of memory.  One suggestion is to increase the
mtry parameter and run the traditional random forest.  The recommended
mtry parameter is typically the square root of the number of
predictors (24 in this case).

Two questions:
(1) is it possible to even get the result using cforest?  What would
it take?  It seems that a 64 bit version may be the only solution.

(2) how large mtry should I try beyond square root of 24?

Thanks,  Albert

Thanks for the suggestion Tony.

This might also be due to the update to R 2.12 which on MS/Windows no longer supports the use of libglade which has been replaced with GtkBuilder (both of which are used to load the XML that defines the Rattle GUI).

Rattle supports both libglade (for backward compatibility) and GtkBuilder. Which one is used is dependent on the crv$useGtkBuilder variable and I try to work out which is the best setting on starting Rattle. But this can be overriden:

> library(rattle)
> crv$useGtkBuilder <- FALSE
> rattle()

The error Ajay is getting is because you are using an older version of the Gtk libraries on MS/Windows (which does not support the "requires" option in the XML file). So the above trick may not fix that. Instead, you will need to install Gtk version  2.16.6. This is available from

 http://downloads.sourceforge.net/gtk-win/gtk2-runtime-2.16.6-2010-02-24-ash.exe

Do let us know if this solves the problem for you Ajay (as Tony mentioned I'm travelling at the moment so it is not quite so easy for me to test this again).

Regards,
Graham

> > library(rattle)
